chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud al-Asadi, from Ibn 'Umar, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:

I heard my father, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام, saying: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Any Muslim man who sits in his place of prayer in which he performed the fajr prayer, remembering Allah until the sun rises, there shall be for him a reward like that of one who performed hajj to the House of Allah, and he shall be forgiven. And if he remains sitting there until there comes an hour in which prayer becomes permissible, then he performs two rak'ahs or four, what has previously passed of his sins shall be forgiven for him, and there shall be for him a reward like that of one who performed hajj to the House of Allah.

key_terms.الْأَجْرِ: divine reward granted for the act
key_terms.بَيْتِ اللَّهِ: the House of Allah, the Ka'bah
key_terms.كَحَاجِّ: like the reward of a pilgrim performing hajj
key_terms.مُصَلَّاهُ: his place of prayer where he performed salat

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for sitting in dhikr after fajr until sunrise?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the merit of remaining in one's place of fajr prayer engaged in dhikr until sunrise. It states that doing so, and then performing prayer when its time becomes permissible, brings immense reward and forgiveness, likened to the reward of hajj to the House of Allah.
